name: Deepprint — Shelf Guerrilla Architecture Collective
description: Deepprint emerged from the Tier 1 Bridgeport Stacks when a loose network of displaced construction workers, failed architecture students, and scrapped-equipment salvagers began illegally modifying derelict structures — adding load-bearing extensions, unauthorized stairwells, and ornate facade overlays using stolen 3D-print slurry and reclaimed rebar. Their signature aesthetic is called 'growthwork': organic-looking structural additions that appear to have erupted from the original building, covered in embedded found objects, cracked ceramic tiles, and weather-sealed graffiti panels. The collective's unofficial quartermaster, Priya Selassie-Okonkwo, maintains a rotating supply network out of a ghost market stall in the Caldwell Underpass. Deepprint has no formal membership — you join by doing, and your work either stands or it doesn't.
cultural_impact: Deepprint has structurally improved several otherwise condemned Shelf blocks, creating de facto community spaces that no corponation sanctioned or funded. City safety enforcement periodically demolishes their additions, but the collective rebuilds faster than inspectors can document violations.
locations: Caldwell Underpass Ghost Market, Bridgeport Stacks
The Extrusion — a Deepprint-modified tenement on Shelf Row 9
story_hooks: A Deepprint addition accidentally stabilizes a building sitting atop a forgotten pre-Collapse data vault — now multiple parties want access and the collective is caught in the middle.
The Unnamed Architect is revealed to be a rogue synthetic urban planner who escaped corporate deletion — and Seam Rights advocates want to use their story publicly, against Deepprint's wishes.
A Tier 4 developer offers to legitimize and fund Deepprint, splitting the collective between those who want resources and those who see it as a co-optation death sentence.
